title: "Diffusion Model"

## Simple explanation

A diffusion model learns to generate data by starting with noise and
gradually transforming it into a sample, such as an image. It learns this
process using examples that have been progressively noised during
training.

## Technical explanation

Diffusion models define a forward noising process and train a model to
estimate or remove noise at different steps. Generation iteratively
applies a learned reverse process, often conditioned on text or other
inputs. Sampling methods and step counts affect quality, diversity, and
latency.

## Why it matters in AI engineering

Diffusion models have enabled high-quality image, audio, and other
generative systems. Engineers must consider sampling cost, conditioning,
data provenance, evaluation, and safety when building applications around
them.

## How it works

Training gradually corrupts data with noise and teaches a neural network
to predict the added noise or a related target. At inference, the model
repeatedly denoises a noise sample according to a chosen sampler to
produce an output.

## Practical example

For text-to-image generation, a model can encode a text prompt and use
that conditioning while denoising an initial latent noise representation
over multiple steps.

## Common misconceptions

- A diffusion model does not retrieve a finished image from a database
  as its generation mechanism.
- More sampling steps do not always improve results enough to justify
  their cost.
- Generated samples can still contain errors, biases, or artifacts.
